info_cards.title: Famous Photograph: View from the Window at Le Gras (the first photograph)
info_cards.fact: "View from the Window at Le Gras (the first photograph)" is a famous photograph, credited to Nicephore Niepce.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Dance
info_cards.fact: "The Dance" by Henri Matisse. Shows five figures dancing in a circle, painted in bold blue, green, and red.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Icarus
info_cards.fact: "Icarus" by Henri Matisse. A paper cut-out artwork from Matisse's Jazz series showing a falling figure among stars.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Snail
info_cards.fact: "The Snail" by Henri Matisse. A large abstract paper cut-out artwork arranged in a spiral like a snail shell.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Peaceable Kingdom
info_cards.fact: "The Peaceable Kingdom" by Edward Hicks. A folk-art painting showing wild and tame animals living together peacefully, inspired by the Bible.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Gulf Stream
info_cards.fact: "The Gulf Stream" by Winslow Homer. Shows a small boat adrift at sea, painted by one of America's leading marine artists.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Snap the Whip
info_cards.fact: "Snap the Whip" by Winslow Homer. Shows a group of barefoot children playing a game outside a one-room schoolhouse.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Washington Crossing the Delaware
info_cards.fact: "Washington Crossing the Delaware" by Emanuel Leutze. A large history painting showing General Washington crossing an icy river.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Oxbow
info_cards.fact: "The Oxbow" by Thomas Cole. A sweeping landscape of the Connecticut River valley by the Hudson River School.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Kindred Spirits
info_cards.fact: "Kindred Spirits" by Asher Brown Durand. Shows two friends standing on a rocky ledge admiring a forest landscape.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Voyage of Life: Childhood
info_cards.fact: "The Voyage of Life: Childhood" by Thomas Cole. Part of a series of four paintings showing a traveller's journey through life stages.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Bull and Bear (Frankfurt)
info_cards.fact: "Bull and Bear (Frankfurt)" by Reinhard Dachlauer. Bronze statues outside the Frankfurt Stock Exchange representing market trends.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Atlas Statue (Paris Opera)
info_cards.fact: "Atlas Statue (Paris Opera)" by Charles Gumery. A gilded statue group atop the Paris Opera House.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Nike of Samothrace replica (Caesars Palace)
info_cards.fact: "Nike of Samothrace replica (Caesars Palace)" by Modern replica sculptors. A faithful replica of the ancient Greek Winged Victory displayed publicly.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Gattamelata
info_cards.fact: "Gattamelata" by Donatello. An early Renaissance equestrian statue honouring a Venetian military commander.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Judith and Holofernes (Donatello)
info_cards.fact: "Judith and Holofernes (Donatello)" by Donatello. A bronze sculpture in Florence depicting a biblical story of courage.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Habakkuk
info_cards.fact: "Habakkuk" by Donatello. A marble prophet statue made for the Florence Cathedral's bell tower.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia (reconstruction model)
info_cards.fact: "The Statue of Zeus at Olympia (reconstruction model)" by Phidias (ancient). One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, known today through historical reconstructions.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Colossus of Rhodes (reconstruction model)
info_cards.fact: "Colossus of Rhodes (reconstruction model)" by Chares of Lindos (ancient). An ancient wonder of the world, known today only through historical descriptions and models.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Statue of Liberty's torch (replica, Paris)
info_cards.fact: "The Statue of Liberty's torch (replica, Paris)" by Frederic Auguste Bartholdi. A smaller replica of the Statue of Liberty stands on a bridge in Paris, France.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Genius of Electricity
info_cards.fact: "Genius of Electricity" by Evelyn Beatrice Longman. A gilded bronze statue once atop a telephone building, symbolizing communication.
